summary: This program is the bakery's front counter: it creates one plain cookie, one decorated cookie, and one gift cookie, prints each one's description through a single shared helper method, then packages the gift cookie with a personal message.

lines.text: Creates an ordinary cookie by passing its flavor to the Cookie constructor.
Creates a decorated cookie, which is a Cookie with extra decorating behavior added by the subclass.
Creates a gift cookie, the subclass that knows how to wrap a cookie for presentation.
Passes the plain cookie to the helper method, which prints it as one line of the menu.
A GiftCookie can be handed to a method that expects a Cookie, because every subclass object is also an object of its parent type.
Calls a method that only GiftCookie has, so the gift message can be attached to the order.
Declaring the parameter as Cookie lets this one method display any kind of cookie, which is the payoff of putting the shared behavior in the parent class.
Each object answers describe() in its own way, so the subclasses print their own richer descriptions even though the code here is identical for all three.
